findings.source_passage: But what is a Gam? You might wear out your index-finger running up and down the columns of dictionaries, and never find the word. Dr. Johnson never attained to that erudition; Noah Webster's ark does not hold it.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'But what is a Gam?'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a distinctively comic, voice-establishing passage—the 'index-finger' image and the jokes about Johnson and Webster's ark are the kind of ironic, learned-yet-playful digression that defines Ishmael's register. Its absence removes a key tonal moment before the formal definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the 'index-finger running up and down the columns of dictionaries' sentence and the Noah Webster's ark quip before the formal GAM definition.

findings.source_passage: Because, in the case of pirates, say, I should like to know whether that profession of theirs has any peculiar glory about it. It sometimes ends in uncommon elevation, indeed; but only at the gallows.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'But look at the godly, honest...'
findings.why_it_matters: The gallows joke and the follow-up about 'no proper foundation for his superior altitude' is a signature Ishmaelean irony—comic syllogism deployed to deflate pirate pretension and reinforce the whaler's dignity. Cutting it flattens the satirical argument.
findings.suggested_fix: After mentioning pirates sneering at spouters, add the gallows elevation joke and the conclusion that the pirate 'has no solid basis to stand on.'

findings.source_passage: godly, honest, unostentatious, hospitable, sociable, free-and-easy whaler!
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'But look at the godly...'
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical accumulation of six adjectives ('godly, honest, unostentatious, hospitable, sociable, free-and-easy') is prosodically distinctive and carries the chapter's celebratory irony about whalemen. The draft trims to three, losing the mock-hymnal cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full six-adjective string verbatim: 'godly, honest, unostentatious, hospitable, sociable, free-and-easy.'

findings.source_passage: mutually cutting each other on the high seas, like a brace of dandies in Broadway; and all the time indulging, perhaps, in finical criticism upon each other's rig.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'finical criticism upon each other's rig' clause is the kicker that makes the dandy simile work as social satire; without it the image loses its comic specificity.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'and all the time indulging, perhaps, in finical criticism upon each other's rig' after the Broadway dandies comparison.

findings.source_passage: this same expressive word has now for many years been in constant use among some fifteen thousand true born Yankees. Certainly, it needs a definition, and should be incorporated into the Lexicon. With that view, let me learnedly define it.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'But what is a Gam?'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Fifteen thousand true born Yankees' and the mock-lexicographic 'should be incorporated into the Lexicon' build the playful scholarly persona; the draft retains only 'let me learnedly define it' without its buildup.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the '15,000 true born Yankees' figure and the 'should be incorporated into the Lexicon' sentence to give 'learnedly define it' its intended ironic weight.

summary: Three medium-severity findings (loss of the dictionary/Johnson/Webster comic passage, loss of the gallows joke, and flattening of the signature six-adjective whaler encomium) collectively trigger regeneration.
